nodes.name: First of the month
nodes.notes: Separate workflow from the pipeline because it runs on a different clock. Tracking polls every six hours; money is computed once a month. Putting both on the same trigger means either paying twelve times too often or tracking twelve times too rarely.

parameters.query:
-- What the previous period came to. Read before anything is written, so the
-- sanity check downstream has something to compare against.
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents), 0)::bigint AS total_cents,
       COUNT(*)::int AS creator_count
FROM payouts
WHERE period_end = $1::date;

nodes.name: Previous period total
nodes.notes: period_end = this period's start, because the intervals are half-open and therefore touch exactly.

parameters.query:
-- Recomputed from posts on every run, never accumulated into a running
-- total. A counter drifts the first time a task runs twice, and drift is
-- invisible until somebody complains.
--
-- Integer cents end to end. (views * rate + 500) / 1000 in integer division
-- is rate-per-thousand rounded half up, with no float anywhere near it:
-- 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3 in binary floating point, and a payout that is off by
-- a cent is a support ticket.
INSERT INTO payouts
  (creator_id, period_start, period_end, post_count, total_views,
   amount_cents, computed_at)
SELECT c.id, $1::date, $2::date,
       COUNT(p.id)::int,
       COALESCE(SUM(p.views), 0),
       (COALESCE(SUM(p.views), 0) * c.rate_cents_per_1k + 500) / 1000,
       now()
FROM creators c
LEFT JOIN posts p
  ON p.creator_id = c.id
  AND p.published_at >= $1::date
  AND p.published_at <  $2::date
WHERE c.status = 'active'
GROUP BY c.id, c.rate_cents_per_1k
-- Nobody is paid for a post nobody saw, and a sub-euro transfer costs more
-- in fees than it moves.
HAVING (COALESCE(SUM(p.views), 0) * c.rate_cents_per_1k + 500) / 1000 >= $3
ON CONFLICT (creator_id, period_start, period_end) DO UPDATE
  SET post_count   = EXCLUDED.post_count,
      total_views  = EXCLUDED.total_views,
      amount_cents = EXCLUDED.amount_cents,
      computed_at  = EXCLUDED.computed_at
RETURNING creator_id, post_count, total_views, amount_cents;

nodes.name: Recompute payouts
nodes.notes: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on (creator, period) makes a second run for the same month an update rather than a second payout. Running this workflow twice by hand is safe, and that is deliberate: the failure mode of an unsafe payout job is that nobody dares re-run it after a partial failure.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ text: `payouts ${$json.period_start} to ${$json.period_end}: ${$json.creators} creator(s), ${(($json.total_cents)/100).toFixed(2)} EUR (last period ${(($json.previous_total_cents)/100).toFixed(2)} EUR)` }) }}

nodes.name: Report the total
nodes.notes: A successful run says what it did. A workflow that is only ever heard from when it breaks is one you stop trusting when it goes quiet, because silence and death look identical.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO dead_letters
  (workflow_id, workflow_name, execution_id, execution_url, node, kind,
   payload, attempts, error, reason)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, 'Sanity check', 'payout', $5::jsonb, 1, $6, 'permanent');

nodes.name: Hold for review
nodes.notes: reason 'permanent', because retrying computes the same suspicious number again. This one needs a person, and the dead letter is how it gets counted instead of scrolled past.

nodes.name: Alert the hold
nodes.notes: Says explicitly that nothing was transferred. An alert that leaves the reader unsure whether money moved gets escalated at 3am whether or not it needed to be.
